title: SFO’s venture in four Honduran airports ended with an estimated $1.45 million loss

beats.text: How did San Francisco end up managing airports in Honduras?

visual.sub: A City-owned company signed up to manage four airports

beats.text: The City owned SFO Enterprises, which formed a Delaware subsidiary in 2000.

visual.kicker: A City-owned company signed up to manage four airports

beats.text: Its Honduran consortium operated four airports.

visual.kicker: A City-owned company signed up to manage four airports

beats.text: Airport staff signed on both sides of the repayment agreements.

visual.kicker: Airport employees worked on both sides of the billing agreement

beats.text: SFO had already provided services for 18 months.

visual.label: Airport employees worked on both sides of the billing agreement

beats.text: The Board left $73,395 available for international services in one year.

visual.kicker: The ledger showed only the budget available after a reserve

beats.text: The next budget called for an exit by January 2004.

visual.kicker: The exit deadline passed before the buyer took over

beats.text: The airport dates the sale 334 days after that target.

visual.label: The exit deadline passed before the buyer took over

beats.text: Part of the sale price depended on future results.

visual.kicker: The contingent sale payment was uncollectible

beats.text: Auditors put the unpaid amount at $787,200.

visual.kicker: The contingent sale payment was uncollectible

beats.text: At the hearing, the airport director expected a loss of about $1.5 million.
